d8bf505e803d53fe7d7514c3fd8717ed60ba5259.summary: A U.S. Department of Justice press release (published 2018-08-01) announces federal indictments in Seattle against three alleged members of FIN7, also called the Carbanak Group and the Navigator Group. The report says FIN7 ran malware campaigns since 2015 against more than 100 U.S. companies, mainly in restaurants, gaming and hospitality, and sold the stolen card data. Three suspects were arrested abroad in 2018 (Germany, Poland, Spain) and are detained pending trial or extradition. The report says the charges are allegations and the defendants are presumed innocent.

d889f8ed2f6a73de74d4c8ec846a60281b64c951.summary: Cisco Talos blog post (published 2018-12-18) on illicit cryptocurrency mining. It describes campaigns by Rocke, the 8220 Mining Group and tor2mine, which exploit internet-facing servers and deliver XMRig-based Monero miners. Talos says the groups shared similar tactics and were first mistakenly seen as one actor, and that together they made hundreds of thousands of dollars. It also notes Rocke began developing destructive malware posing as ransomware as cryptocurrency values fell.

d8c342f73b2603fedc4913e6a2378a846331fa96.summary: This is a Linux documentation page (a how-to on Linux kernel modules, LKMs) explaining how to insert and remove them with insmod, rmmod, modprobe and depmod, how module dependencies and loading errors work, and how /proc/modules is read. It describes no threat actor, campaign, malware, vulnerability or incident, so it is not a threat report.

d8141e5ae73b0856feae51f1c3dd07a979f15ad0.summary: FortiGuard Labs (Fortinet) report on RapperBot, an IoT malware family tracked since June 2022. It reuses Mirai source code but brute-forces SSH servers rather than Telnet. Later samples added persistence through SSH keys and a hidden root account, and the bot has a minimal set of DoS attacks. Over 3,500 scanner IPs were observed, half from the US, Taiwan and South Korea. The report says the primary motivation is still unclear.
